text:
maya: FYI rolled rwdv3-quant8 to 30% for the summarization routes overnight. quick A/B shows aggregate BLEU up +0.9 but the 'enterprise-long' slice is -4.3% which is worrying.

rohit: ah. did the canary rules trigger an autofallback?

infra-bot: rollout rwdv3-quant8 -> 30% complete at 1801109000. no autofallback events recorded.

laura: paste of per-slice deltas from last 6h window:
```
enterprise-long: -0.043 (n=2.3k)
customer-support: +0.012 (n=38k)
faq: +0.007 (n=15k)
internal-notes: -0.001 (n=4k)
```

maya: enterprise-long is 2.3k samples in 6h, that's high-value traffic (SLAs). our current rule is global BLEU drop >1.5% AND any weighted-slice <-2% => fallback. enterprise-long weight is 0.03 so global didn't hit.

rohit: okay so the low weight buried it. we discussed per-slice absolute cutoffs before. propose: add a per-slice hard cutoff if |delta| >= 3.5% AND slice_samples >= 500 in the window => immediate rollback for that slice's traffic.

laura: +1. also add a sustained window check: require delta persist over 3 consecutive 10m windows to avoid noise.

maya: good. also suggested: for enterprise customers, allow customer-weight override that increases slice weight for rollout decisions without changing metric aggregation used for product experiments.

rohit: how about smoothing/prior shrinkage? current prior = 0.5% shrink over 6h. for first 12h post-promote reduce shrink to 0.1% so the signal reacts faster.

laura: agree. and add a minimum-effect-size requirement: delta / sqrt(variance/n) > 1.2 to avoid tiny but significant deltas from flipping.

infra-bot: note: config preview generated at https://config.redwood.ai/rollouts/preview/789 (internal).

maya: test plan: run contrastive judge on 3k enterprise-long pairs, run offline user-sim retention proxy for that customer cohort, and smokecheck on edge cases (very long inputs).

rohit: i ran a quick contrastive sample (n=500) earlier — rwdv2 wins 58% vs rwdv3 on long enterprise docs. that's aligned with the BLEU drop.

maya: decision: pause ramp to 30% -> hold at 10% for the enterprise routes, open hotfix PR to add hard cutoff + sustained-window + prior tweak. label PR "rollout: per-slice hard cutoff for high-value slices".

laura: please include a migration step: existing rollout records need new metadata for 'customer_weight' to be backfilled from tags. add a DB migration in the PR.

rohit: i'll review the PR. also adding a Datadog monitor: redwood.rollout.slice.delta (enterprise-long) alert if <= -2.5% over 30m to eng-oncall but set as non-pager for first 24h.

pagerbot: monitor created -> ID db-00123. severity LOW. initial sensitivity silenced for 24h.

maya: timeline: PR -> review (rohit) within 2h, merge -> ops deploy policy -> observe 4h. if per-slice cutoff hits, ops will automatically fallback that slice and annotate the rollout with incident id.

laura: i'll start the contrastive judge run and paste results.

rohit: quick ask: add an escape hatch for manual disable per-customer so sales/CS can opt-out a rollback for a specific account while we mitigate? but require approval flow.

maya: ok add manual disable flag gated by two approvers. document process in runbook.

laura: contrastive 3k started. current quick sample (n=300) shows v2 wins 60% on longform. will upload full result link when done.

maya: thanks. main lesson: low-weight slices still matter if they map to high-value customers. per-slice absolute cutoffs + sustained-window + temporary prior shrink should reduce blind spots.

rohit: +1. i'll push a draft PR and tag you both.

infra-bot: rollout policy diff created: https://git.redwood.ai/r/redwood/rollouts/commit/ae4b (internal).
